name: Japanese · Phrases · Small talk
source: Phrases: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org) sentences written by native speakers, each linked in its src; lines marked generated were written for Lianki and checked for natural use

entries.reading: いいてんきですね
entries.note: Classic opener with neighbours, shop owners or someone you're waiting with.

entries.reading: きょうはあついですね
entries.note: Small talk in summer; the other person usually just agrees: 本当ですね.

entries.reading: さむいですね
entries.note: Winter opener with anyone, from coworkers to the person at the bus stop.

entries.reading: きょうはむしあついね
entries.note: Among friends in Japan's sticky summer.

entries.reading: あめがふりそうですね
entries.note: Said looking at the sky; a safe, polite remark to anyone.

entries.term: 早く梅雨明けないかなあ。
entries.reading: はやくつゆあけないかなあ
entries.back: I wish the rainy season would end.
entries.note: A very Japanese June–July grumble between friends.

entries.reading: さいきんどう
entries.note: Easy catch-up question to a friend you haven't talked to lately.

entries.reading: しごとはどう
entries.note: To a friend or relative; expect a short answer like まあまあ.

entries.reading: さいきんいそがしいの
entries.note: To a friend you haven't heard from; slightly concerned, friendly.

entries.reading: あいかわらずいそがしいよ
entries.note: Common reply to 最近どう？ or 忙しい？

entries.term: 最近何かいいことあった？
entries.reading: さいきんなにかいいことあった
entries.note: Light question to get a friend talking.

entries.reading: きょうはどうだった
entries.note: Family or partner, in the evening.

entries.reading: しゅうまつはどうだった
entries.note: Monday chat with friends or close coworkers.

entries.reading: こんしゅうまつはなにするの
entries.back: What are you up to this weekend?
entries.note: To a friend or coworker toward the end of the week.

entries.reading: こんしゅうまつあいてる
entries.note: Usually leads into an invitation.

entries.reading: よいしゅうまつを
entries.note: Said on Friday when parting from coworkers or acquaintances.

entries.term: 普段、休みの日は何をしてるの？
entries.reading: ふだんやすみのひはなにをしてるの
entries.back: What do you usually do on your days off?
entries.note: Getting-to-know-you question among peers.

entries.reading: しゅみはなんですか
entries.back: What do you do for fun?
entries.note: Standard polite question on a first meeting; answer 趣味は〜です.

entries.term: 最近何かはまってることある？
entries.reading: さいきんなにかはまってることある
entries.note: Casual way to ask about hobbies, shows, games, food trends.

entries.term: 最近何か面白い映画見た？
entries.reading: さいきんなにかおもしろいえいがみた
entries.note: Easy topic between friends.

entries.term: お仕事は何をされているんですか？
entries.reading: おしごとはなにをされているんですか
entries.back: What do you do for work?
entries.note: Polite, to someone you've just met at a party or event.

entries.term: どこに住んでいるんですか？
entries.reading: どこにすんでいるんですか
entries.note: Usually answered with a neighbourhood or nearest station.

entries.reading: にほんははじめてですか
entries.back: Is this your first time in Japan?
entries.note: What Japanese people often ask visitors.

entries.reading: にほんはどうですか
entries.note: Common friendly question to visitors and newcomers.

entries.term: 日本語がお上手ですね。
entries.reading: にほんごがおじょうずですね
entries.note: A compliment learners hear a lot; reply いえいえ、まだまだです.

entries.reading: そうなんだ
entries.note: The everyday listening response among friends.

entries.reading: そうなんですか
entries.note: Polite listening response showing interest.

entries.reading: へえしらなかった
entries.note: Reacting to new information from a friend.

entries.reading: ほんとう
entries.note: Quick surprised reaction; in speech often ほんと？

entries.reading: いいなあ
entries.note: Mild, friendly envy when a friend shares good news or a trip.

entries.reading: たしかに
entries.note: Agreeing with something a friend said; very common in chat too.
